message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it was right or wrong for me to delete my stepbrother's profile on my Nintendo Switch. Let me start by going through the situation step by step. First, I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom were on a trip. I brought my Switch because my school is more than an hour away, and I wanted something to do during the train commute. My stepbrother really wanted to play on it, so I made a new profile for him to keep his games separate from mine. That worked well because it helped distract him while I studied. When I got back to school, I started getting annoyed because every time I wanted to play a game or go to the eShop, I had to switch back to my profile. It was a minor inconvenience, but it annoyed me enough that I just deleted his profile. I thought it was no big deal because I usually don't bring my Switch over when I visit. Then, during Thanksgiving, I brought my Switch again for the train ride. My stepbrother picked it up and started playing. He came into the kitchen where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone. He wanted me to help him fix it, and when I told him I deleted it, he started crying, though not full-on crying, just his eyes were watery and red. Now he's shut up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because he knew my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. So, was it right or wrong for me to delete his profile? Let me think about the different aspects. On one hand, the Switch is my property. I have the right to manage who uses it and how. I created the profile to keep things organized, but when it became a hassle for me, I deleted it. I didn't think it was a big deal because I don't usually bring it over, so I didn't anticipate him using it again. On the other hand, my stepbrother was using the profile, and when I deleted it, it caused him emotional distress. He was upset because he lost his progress in Zelda, which is a significant game for him. My dad also thinks it was mean, which adds another layer of concern. I should consider the impact of my actions. Deleting the profile without discussing it with my stepbrother or my dad was impulsive. It caused him to feel hurt and upset, which is not something I want to contribute to, especially within my family. Maybe I should have communicated better. If I was annoyed by the profile, I could have talked to my stepbrother about it or found another way to manage the profiles without deleting his. That way, I could have maintained the Switch's organization without causing emotional harm. I also need to think about the trust aspect. By deleting his profile, I might have made him feel like I didn't respect his space or his interests. Trust is important, especially in a family setting, and my actions might have damaged that trust. In the future, it would be better to approach such situations with more communication and empathy. Instead of acting impulsively, taking a moment to discuss the issue could prevent hurt feelings and maintain a positive relationship. So, considering all these points, I think it was wrong to delete his profile without discussing it first. It caused unnecessary emotional distress and could have been handled more respectfully and considerately.
